lines.text: Project time! Today you will join everything from this module into one report that almost builds itself, with you checking at every important step.
You now have three tools: templates, a self-updating dashboard, and a script that emails you.
A report pipeline joins them, from data in to message out.
Each step hands its result to the next one.
A checkpoint is a planned stop where a person looks before the work moves on.
Put one after cleaning, one after the numbers, and one before anything leaves your inbox.
The automation sends drafts to you, and you send the final version to others.
Give the AI only the dashboard numbers, not the full order list.
Ask it to use only those numbers, to say up or down correctly, and to add no reasons of its own.
Then compare every number in its draft with the dashboard.
Each week, write the date, the minutes taken including checks, and any problem you caught.
Also count the setup time, and work out how many weeks it takes to pay back.
After a month, you have honest proof to show your manager.
Start on paper: draw every step of the report, from data in to message out.
Mark three checkpoints, after cleaning, after the numbers, and before anything is sent.
The script only ever emails you, and you decide what goes to your manager.
We give Copilot only the dashboard numbers, never the full order list.
The note is short and clear, but checkpoint C finds two problems.
The rise is about eight point seven percent, not twelve percent.
And the reason about Veg Thali was invented, because we never gave the AI any reasons.
This script reads the dashboard cells exactly as they appear on screen.
If the dashboard is empty, it stops and sends nothing at all.
It emails you one draft, with a reminder of what to check before forwarding.
Run the same seven-point check from lesson three before you use it.
Honest measuring means counting checking time and setup time too.
In our example, the report drops from seventy-five minutes to twenty.
The setup took one hundred and fifty minutes, so it pays for itself in about three weeks.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now plan it, build it, test it, and share it!
